title: Three Ways of Storing and Accessing Lots of Images in Python
description: Compare three ways of storing images in Python, as PNG files on disk, in LMDB, and in HDF5, with timings for reading and writing lots of images.
summary: Why would you want to know more about different ways of storing and accessing images in Python? If you’re segmenting a handful of images by color or detecting faces one by one using OpenCV, then you don’t need to worry about it.
takeaways: ImageNet is a well-known public image database put together for training models on tasks like object classification, detection, and segmentation, and it consists of over 14 million images.
Even if you’re using the Python Imaging Library (PIL) to draw on a few hundred photos, you still don’t need to.
Think about how long it would take to load all of them into memory for training, in batches, perhaps hundreds or thousands of times.
